The engine includes a wiring harness, various sensors, and plastic intake components.

claims.evidence: The Lexus LX series typically uses 470 or 570 designations; LX460 is not a standard model name, though LS460 and GX460 exist.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical failure or seized components.
risks.proof: A video showing the crankshaft being rotated manually with a tool.
A clear photo of the engine code stamped onto the metal engine block (e.g., 1UR, 2UZ, 3UR).
risks.if_unproven: as a generic unidentified V8 engine

risks.risk: Damaged or cut wiring harness and broken sensors.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all electrical connectors and the main wiring loom.
risks.if_unproven: as having a damaged harness requiring replacement

proof_requests: Photo of the engine code stamped on the engine block.
Video of the engine being turned over manually to prove it is not seized.
Clear photos of the ECU part number if included.
Close-up photos of the wiring harness plugs.
response.reason: The seller cites a model (LX460) that does not exist in the Lexus lineup, creating significant ambiguity about whether this is an LS460, GX460, or a misidentified LX470 engine. A photo of the engine code on the block is required to establish identity and value.
